correctness.rationale: Exact acceptance-chain rates ab,ac,bc are correct; tagged rare-part survival is bounded at each min(a,b)=s by probability at least 1/(s+r) of matching, giving the telescoping product (h+r-1)/(n+r). The A/B imbalance never exceeds r; each rare attachment differs from a fair coin by at most r/(4h), leading by coupling to the stated TV bound. After the rare vertices are used, remaining AB matching leaves the absolute coin imbalance. Choosing \(h\sim\sqrt{nr}\) and applying the binomial CLT proves both scaling claims. Independent labeled-vertex and edge-permutation finite-state checks passed.

value.rationale: Adding a finite dilute third sublattice to the perfectly jammable balanced complete bipartite substrate produces a nontrivial macroscopic probability of a local jamming defect (for r=2, two vacant vertices with limiting probability 1/2), while coverage density alone would hide it. The result provides all fixed-r vacancy distributions, an explicit convergence error and the emerging half-normal crossover for many dilute vertices, tied to a clear physical irreversible adsorption mechanism rather than a cosmetic finite graph computation.
